In this lesson you will identify the type of operational amplifier circuit and determine if the circuit is faulted and if so, what the fault is.
INTRODUCTIONM
You will practice troubleshooting four types of operational amplifier circuits:
Non-Inverting, Inverting, Difference and Summing
For simplicity, only DC voltage inputs will be used. Remember, operational amplifiers can use AC inputs, however, the only difference in troubleshooting is the type of test equipment used.
Non-Inverting, Inverting, Difference and Summing

In each troubleshooting practice problem, you will be asked to: Identify the type of operational amplifier circuit. 2. Calculate the voltage gain. 3. Determine if the circuit is operating correctly. 4. Identify the probable fault.
1. Identify the type of operational amplifier circuit.
3. Determine if the circuit is operating correctly.

OP AMP TS PRACTICEE

The purpose of this experiment is to give you practice in troubleshooting various operational amplifier circuits. If the circuit is faulted, you will determine the faulty component and verify correct operation when the computer repairs the circuit...
EXPERIMENT
Pick up the PC130-54 card. Compare the card with the schematic shown.
This card is used to give you practice in troubleshooting various operational amplifier circuits.
IC1 is an operational amplifier that can be configured for a non-inverting, inverting, difference or summing amplifier.
Switch S5 is used to configure the Op Amp. In the SUM (UP) position the Op Amp is a summing amplifier or inverting amp (R4 fully CCW).
S5 in the DIFF (DOWN) position configures the Op Amp a difference amp or non-inverting amplifier with R1 fully CCW.
S1 and S2 select the type of input signal used, AC, +DC, -DC.
S3 and S4 select different values of input resistors that effect the gain of the Op Amp. Let's start the experiment.
